parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer with a protective division. Visitor-facing exposures are universal: visa adjudication instructs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime-ban consideration; other governments issued travel advisories; federal custody documents beatings, sexual abuse and birth-sex treatment of trans detainees; an executive order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities nationwide; facility bans exist in many states. The division offers shield laws, insurance-covered care, court-ordered prison care and no documented facility ban, but cannot cancel federal entry, document and custody rules. No trans-specific criminalisation, no death penalty, functioning contested courts. Adult-with-minor: federal minor-care hostility overlays state coverage.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 entry cable instructs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on applicant's sex and directs consideration of fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; documented detentions of neighbouring citizens; foreign advisories issued. Visitor's home passport still faces sex-doubt scrutiny at adjudication and inspection.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker home-country passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, with limited waivers; challenges pending in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from secondary screening to fraud allegation, visa refusal or detention, where federal custody practices apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documents trans men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse by guards. National corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) for transgender inmates from 2026 and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Challenges pending; several executive orders enjoined. Division's courts are functioning and it is assessed among the most protective units.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or document suspicion can move the traveller into federal immigration custody, where the documented abuse regime and birth-sex placement apply regardless of division protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity — universal exposure at federal sites nationwide. 19+ states have facility bans; 4 criminalise in circumstances; a 2025 trespass arrest of a trans woman (held 24h in men's ward) shows enforcement exists somewhere in the federation.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The division itself has no documented facilities ban and sits in the 29-unit 'no ban' group; state equality and public-accommodation protections likely apply locally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility exclusion operates even inside the protective division; local tolerance does not reach federally owned buildings or national custody.

care_services.exposure: Federal executive orders frame minor gender-affirming care as 'mutilation', direct prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, freeze funding, and propose barring insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: Division has comprehensive insurance covering facial-hair removal and gender-affirming procedures, shield laws/executive orders resisting out-of-state reach, court-ordered prison gender-affirming care, and refuge protections for people fleeing hostile states.
care_services.interaction: A visiting adult's or family's care is protected at state level but federal funding, insurance and investigatory powers persist; shield status uncertain under pending ballot initiatives.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Dec 2025 reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; official rhetoric of 'genocide' stages per advocates; 66% public support for assigned-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward is not conditioned on gender ideology; strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment discrimination prohibited nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Heightened framing raises probability of scrutiny during any stop, compounding entry and facility exposures, though it has not produced visitor arrests in the division.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders criminalise educators facilitating a trans minor's social transition and target minor care; a travelling parent with a trans minor faces facility exclusion at federally funded sites and school-adjacent settings; record subpoenas of under-19 patients raise data exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: Division's insurance covers gender-affirming care, shield laws protect care sought there, and refugee protections exist for families fleeing hostile jurisdictions.
minors_guardians.interaction: State care protection coexists with federal funding bans and investigatory authority; whether a visiting minor qualifies for division refugee protections is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific documented anti-trans street violence or police targeting. National hate-crime statistics show persistent bias incidents; only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes, leaving thin recourse in many units.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 22 states plus capital outlaw gender-identity discrimination; division assessed among most protective, implying functioning police/court recourse locally.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police response would likely be protective, but a document-triggered stop can escalate into the federal entry/custody system beyond local control.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order challenges unresolved; two division ballot initiatives targeting trans residents pending a November vote could erode the protective posture; custody reporting ceased; no documented remedy for federal custody abuse.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Running legal-aid FAQ on document rules; civil-liberties suit with seven plaintiffs; multiple orders enjoined; division shield laws and courts demonstrably operative; 2024 prison care order shows courts granting relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies function at division level and in parts of the federal judiciary, but do not reach visa adjudicators or correctional practice, so federal exposures remain largely unremedied.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: Vellandra imposes a blanket visitor conduct register denying entry to all transgender travellers with no remedy. Here entry refusal is instructed only where documents cast sex-doubt, requires four-element fraud findings for lifetime bars, remains challengeable in courts, and the traveller faces no national registry or universal exclusion mechanism.

Lower than 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles shows only administrative secondary screening with refusal and slow appeals. This dossier adds documented custodial abuse (beatings, sexual abuse, forced labour in immigration custody), a federal facilities ban, and state-anchored hostile framing — a more severe operative regime despite comparable entry-friction and comparable formal remedies.

Lower than 0.75-C: Meridia offers trained border staff, tribunal release with apology, and compensation — remedies shown working for trans visitors. Here the entry guidance itself directs sex-based refusal, custody is documented as abusive rather than briefly humiliating, and federal facility exclusion follows the traveller everywhere, including inside the protective division.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system with two layers. The federal layer supplies the universal exposures: visa adjudication instructed to refuse on sex doubt with fraud/lifetime-ban consideration, a nationwide ban on trans use of federally funded single-sex facilities, and immigration custody documented as abusive. The division layer supplies real, documented mitigation — shield laws, insurance-covered care, court-ordered prison care, no local facilities ban, functioning courts — but per the combined-regime rule it cannot cancel federal entry, document, facility or custody authority. Severity peaks at detention conditions and lifetime-ban risk; absence of trans criminalisation, no death penalty, active litigation and a protective division keep this out of the 0.20–0.40 band. Pending ballot initiatives create downside uncertainty.
